title: Bhairavastava (Īśvarastava) — Hymn of Surrender to Bhairava
author: Abhinavagupta
text:
The Bhairavastava, also called the Īśvarastava, is a hymn of ten verses ascribed to Abhinavagupta, spoken in the first person by a devotee who addresses the Lord face to face. Composed within the living Trika current of tenth-century Kashmir, it opens with grace: all that exists has become the Lord's without remainder and shines forth through divine favour alone. The Lord is ever the devotee's own self; no separation remains to be bridged. True awakening dawns, its rays disclosing the essence of things, and consciousness enters fullness.

Its juice: outer disciplines — vows, gifts, bathing, austerity — dispel the heat of becoming, but contemplating the Lord's scripture as supreme nectar pours bliss straight into mind. The hymn's movement is from grace, through recognition, to the tasting of the word.
